note: CKEditor Accordion (Detail Plugin) adds a CKEditor 5 toolbar item 'detail' (label 'Add accordion', plugin ckeditor_details_detail / JS detail.Detail) that inserts a native <details>/<summary>/<div class="details-wrapper"> accordion. No module config (configure=null); you enable it per text format by adding 'detail' to the CKEditor 5 toolbar, stored in editor.editor.<format> settings.toolbar.items. Medium/hard cases create namespaced CKEditor5 formats (ckd_*) and read/verify the 'detail' toolbar item in the live editor config.

evals.prompt: The ckeditor_details module adds an 'Add accordion' button to CKEditor 5. What HTML does it insert when an editor clicks it?
evals.expected_output: It inserts a native HTML5 disclosure widget: a <details> element containing a <summary> and a <div class="details-wrapper"> body, which browsers render as a click-to-expand accordion with no runtime JavaScript.

evals.prompt: How do I enable the ckeditor_details accordion button for a text format on a Drupal 11 site, and what is the toolbar item's machine name? Is there a module settings page?
evals.expected_output: There is no module settings page (configure=null). On Text formats and editors (/admin/config/content/formats), edit a CKEditor 5 format and drag the Detail button into its toolbar; the toolbar item machine name is 'detail'. It is stored in editor.editor.<format> at settings.toolbar.items.

evals.prompt: After adding the ckeditor_details accordion button to a text format that restricts allowed HTML, the accordion markup gets stripped on save. What HTML elements must the format allow for the accordion to survive?
evals.expected_output: The format's Limit allowed HTML tags filter must permit the elements the plugin declares: <details>, <summary>, <div>, and <div class="details-wrapper">. Otherwise filter_html strips the accordion markup.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, one CKEditor 5 text format has the accordion (detail) button in its toolbar. Inspect the live editor configuration and name that text format.
evals.expected_output: The format is ckd_known: editor.editor.ckd_known settings.toolbar.items includes 'detail'.

evals.prompt: This site has two CKEditor 5 text formats, ckd_on and ckd_off. Exactly one has the accordion (detail) button enabled in its toolbar. Inspect the live configuration and state which one.
evals.expected_output: ckd_on has the accordion button: editor.editor.ckd_on settings.toolbar.items includes 'detail', while ckd_off's toolbar does not.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a CKEditor 5 text format named ckd_task that does not yet have the accordion button. Using the ckeditor_details module, add the accordion (detail) button to that format's toolbar. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: editor.editor.ckd_task settings.toolbar.items contains 'detail' (the format still uses the ckeditor5 editor).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a new text format with machine name ckd_new that uses CKEditor 5 and includes the accordion button (from the ckeditor_details module) in its toolbar, so editors using it can insert collapsible sections. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A filter format ckd_new exists with a CKEditor 5 editor (editor.editor.ckd_new editor=ckeditor5) whose settings.toolbar.items contains 'detail'.
